newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Feb 26.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Shares ended a choppy session down but well above its lows as investors continued, at least for the time being, to discount Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's attempts to pour cold water on a fired-up equities market. The FTSE 100 index closed 15.4 points lower at 4,329.3.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended in positive territory, recovering quickly from a brief sharp slide after Greenspan raised the chilling prospect of an interest rate rise. The IBIS DAX index ended up 11.68 points at 3,245.02 points, having dropped to a low of 3,216.94 points immediately after Greenspan's comments. Earlier, The 30-share DAX index rose 4.66 points to end the floor session at 3,237.87 points.

PARIS - Stocks closed lower, knocked back into negative territory after Greenspan said he could not rule out a pre-emptive rate increase to head off inflation. After starting in the red, the French market managed to eke out a 0.35 percent gain at one point but dropped after Greenspan's remarks to Congress. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 5.55 points, or 0.21 percent, at 2,602.17.

ZURICH - Shares posted a record close, but ended below the day's highs as early losses on Wall Street led to profit-taking in late trade. Volume was very high. Dealers said Novartis, subscription rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals and UBS were in the limelight. Ciba rights were making their bourse debut. The All-share SPI ended up 15.16 points at 2,876.68.

TOKYO - Stocks ended on a weak note, pushed lower by profit taking in both banking-sector and some blue-chip shares in afternoon trade. Brokers said the market lacked direction and trade was very thin with investors staying on the sidelines. The 225-share Nikkei average fell 79.15 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 18,990.92.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended firm but off the day's highs as the Hang Seng Index bumped against resistance and another record-setting rally by HSBC Holdings Plc lost steam. The Hang Seng Index rose 21.57 points, or 0.16 percent, at 13,541.83 after rising to a high of 13,610.43.

SYDNEY - The share market ended lower, weighed down by soft base metals prices and worries about possible Wall Street weakness later in the day. The All Ordinaries index shed 17.7 points to 2,483.1. Brokers said losses by the end of the day had extended across the board as investors began to doubt that Wall Street could make it three rises in a row.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares ended marginally firmer on the back of a bullish gold price and a steady rand. But industrial shares took a knock on the back of profit-taking and a recent spate of poor company results reported by some industrial heavyweights. The industrial index closed 46.7 points down at 8,378.8, while the gold index gained 4.9 points to 1,543.4, leaving the overall index 2.9 points higher at 7,205.7.
